gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 13 build now compiles both the landed libfs starter tests and the new reviewability gate so the helper lane stays honest as it grows.
The existing make target keeps the bounded libfs starter and reviewability checks runnable through the same repeatable path as the other Zigux tranche checkpoints.

The landed starter already mirrors the pure helper-facing shape of simple_statfs(), always_delete_dentry(), and simple_lookup() without claiming live dcache mutation, inode locking, or VFS registration.

Dedicated starter tests keep the current wrapper honest around split fsid packing, default statfs values, negative-dentry discard intent, casefold passthrough, buffer-copy accounting, seek-policy bounds, and directory-emit handoff bookkeeping.
The slice note records the narrow boundary of the landed helper lab so the lane does not overstate itself as live libfs or VFS parity.
A dedicated reviewability gate ties the current starter, tests, slice note, and survey note together so future runs can confirm the lane state before widening helper coverage.
The survey note now describes the landed starter truthfully and keeps the remaining gap around directory iteration, offset policy, and deeper VFS state explicit.

The libfs helper lab now models the early seek-policy surface from dcache_dir_lseek() and offset_dir_llseek() in pure planning form, including SEEK_SET and SEEK_CUR handling, negative-offset rejection, max-position bounds, and whether a positive-entry scan would become necessary.

The libfs helper lab now adds one tiny dcache_readdir()-adjacent emit planner that models the dir_emit_dots() handoff, the transition into positive entry scanning, emitted-entry position accounting, and the early stop case before any live cursor dentries or inode-backed state are touched.

The libfs helper lab now models the pure `simple_transaction_get()` acquire path, including the page-bounded staging-buffer size limit, the single-write-per-open guard, and the empty-response starting state before any live file-local publish, read, or release behavior is claimed.

The next honest transaction-family step is a tiny `simple_transaction_set()` publish planner that keeps the work in response-size validation and publish bookkeeping before any live readback or release state is modeled.
